_comment: Byte-exact encode/decode pairs for the Pico->ESP SAFETY_CMD_GET_STATUS (0x01) payload, per docs/LINK_PROTOCOL.md sec 6, Frame A -- the existing 23-byte layout (SAFETY_LINK_STATUS_FRAME_LEN). payload_hex is the raw command payload as it would sit inside kilnlink_frame_t.payload -- see frame_vectors.json for the outer envelope. Generated by hand-computing struct.pack('<f') in Python and cross-checked against kilnlink_status_encode/decode in test/test_status.c.

vectors.name: healthy_reading
vectors.note: flags = ESTOP|RELAY|ENABLED|TEMP_VALID (0x3C) -- e-stop released... actually ESTOP bit set here just exercises the bit path; see LINK_PROTOCOL.md sec 6 for what each bit means. Both temperatures valid, all three currents nonzero.

vectors.name: temp_invalid_sends_nan_not_zero
vectors.note: TEMP_VALID (bit 5) is clear -- LINK_PROTOCOL.md sec 6 Frame A: 'Send NaN, never 0, when TEMP_VALID is clear.' Both temperature fields are NaN despite the flags byte being 0; currents are legitimately zero (no relay energized) and are NOT NaN -- only the two temperature fields have the NaN-not-zero rule.

hostile_vectors.name: too_short
hostile_vectors.note: 22 bytes -- one short of the fixed 23-byte frame. This frame has no length field of its own to lie about; the wire length itself is the only signal, so a decoder must reject anything that isn't exactly 23 bytes.

hostile_vectors.name: too_long
hostile_vectors.note: 24 bytes -- one more than the fixed 23-byte frame. Equally invalid; this is a fixed-size frame, not a minimum size.

hostile_vectors.name: wrong_cmd
hostile_vectors.note: Byte 0 is 0x08 (DIAG's id), not 0x01 -- an otherwise well-formed 23-byte buffer whose command byte says it's a different frame.
